subject: music
title: Exposition: First and Second Subjects
welcome_lead: Tonic, transition, dominant or relative major — and a codetta.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: sonata-form exposition and tonal plan.

concepts.def: Tripartite Classical form: exposition, development, recapitulation.
First main section: presents two themes in contrasting keys.
Opening theme, in the tonic key.
Modulating passage linking first to second subject.
Contrasting theme, in dominant (major-key works) or relative major (minor-key).

walkthroughs.body_html: The exposition presents: first subject (tonic), transition (modulates), second subject (dominant in major; relative major in minor), and a codetta closing the section.
For a piece in C major: 1st subject C major, 2nd subject G major. For a piece in A minor: 1st subject A minor, 2nd subject C major (relative major).
The exposition is conventionally repeated in Classical sonata movements. Some modern performances omit the repeat — but the formal architecture assumes it.
